To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is a need for methodological reflections on the use of qualitative methods in development studies; and that (2) there is a gap in the literature in terms of the use of qualitative research methods in development studies.
1) The methods used by the researchers in the studies were mainly qualitative and included interviews, participant observations and document analysis.
(1) The methods used by researchers are influenced by the disciplinary background of the researcher, but also by the research question.

how the global and local are entangled in the everyday life and in the politics of the global South, and how this is related to development, power and inequality.
the ways in which development is produced, and how it shapes and is shaped by power relations.
the social, political, economic and cultural aspects of development and change, with a focus on the global South

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are concerned about the methodological choices and challenges in our field of study, and we want to contribute to a discussion on method/ology.
we are concerned with the ways in which the methods we use are shaped and constrained by the theoretical and epistemological positions we adopt.
we have tried to develop a more nuanced and reflective approach to qualitative methods, which we have tried to communicate in our teaching.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method/ological choices we make in research are not neutral. They have implications for what we learn and how we learn, and for how we can communicate and disseminate our research.
qualitative research methods are often not well understood, and that the methods section in many articles is not very informative about the methodological choices made.
the methods we use should be grounded in the theoretical and epistemological foundations of our research questions, and that we need to be aware of the implications of the choices we make.
